headline: US BACKS CRITICAL MINERALS WITH $389M — DOE Targets Rare Earth Processing, Fusion Tech and Advanced Chips to Break China's Supply Chain Lock
snippet: Washington committed $389 million on October 22 to high-purity mineral processing, nuclear fusion technology, and advanced power chips — a direct policy signal that the US government is accelerating domestic critical mineral supply chains ahead of expected rare earth, uranium, and battery metal shortfalls. The funding is aimed at sectors where Chinese state producers currently control more than 80% of global refining output, and for junior mining investors it signals structured government procurement demand for domestically produced critical minerals over the next 3-5 years rather than relying solely on spot market pricing to justify project development capital.

headline: SILVER CRASHES THROUGH $55 FLOOR — FXStreet Bears Now Target $50 as Monthly Decline Hits 13% and Gold-Silver Ratio Explodes to 73
snippet: Spot silver broke below the key $55-per-ounce technical support level on the evening of October 22, with FXStreet now targeting $50 as the next significant support following a 13% monthly decline that puts silver at its lowest since April 2026. The gold-silver ratio widened to approximately 73 — its highest since August — as silver underperformed even gold's own rate-fear selloff, a divergence that historically resolves sharply once the rate catalyst peaks. For silver-focused junior explorers and developers, the drawdown from January's $121 record is now approximately 54%, compressing valuations across the silver junior space ahead of the October 27-28 FOMC clearing event.

headline: CERRO DE PASCO CONSOLIDATES 100% OF QUIULACOCHA TAILINGS — Final Acquisition Secures All Surface Rights on Peru's Largest Polymetallic Tailings Project
snippet: Cerro de Pasco Resources acquired the final remaining portion of the Quiulacocha tailings in Peru on October 21, consolidating 100% ownership and securing all surface rights on a deposit containing an estimated 225 million tonnes of historic silver-zinc-lead tailings from over a century of Peruvian mining. The acquisition removes the last third-party land tenure overhang on what management argues is one of the most compelling environmental remediation and polymetallic resource recovery opportunities in Latin American mining, positioning the company to advance permitting and feasibility work toward a production decision that would also remediate a major legacy environmental liability in the Cerro de Pasco region.

headline: MINAURUM SILVER DISCOVERS BLIND AFRICA VEIN ZONE AT ALAMOS — New High-Grade Vein Expands Sonora Mexico System to 27 Identified Structures
snippet: Minaurum Silver Inc. (TSXV: MGG) announced the discovery of the high-grade Africa vein zone at its 100%-owned Alamos silver project in Sonora, Mexico on October 22, adding a new blind vein discovery — one with no prior surface expression — to a system that has now grown to at least 27 identified vein structures. The Africa zone carries similar structural and mineralogical characteristics to the highest-grade veins at Alamos, which have historically returned multi-kilogram silver intercepts, and the discovery expands the lateral footprint of the project at a time when Minaurum is advancing a maiden resource estimate on one of Mexico's most systematically drilled silver exploration properties.

headline: PROSPECTOR METALS DRILLS 41.34 G/T AU OVER 7.81M IN YUKON TESS ZONE — Best Subinterval Hits 130.77 G/T Over 2.25M
snippet: Prospector Metals Corp (TSXV: PPP) extended the high-grade Tess Zone at its Minto project in the Yukon with hole ML26-056 returning 41.34 g/t gold over 7.81 metres, including 130.77 g/t gold over 2.25 metres — confirming a shallow, high-grade, structurally controlled gold system in a territory that is attracting increasing exploration capital as majors accelerate their hunt for district-scale discoveries near the historic Minto and Keno Hill camps. The intercept adds to a growing body of high-grade drill data at Tess Zone that is building the geological case for a maiden resource estimate.

headline: ALKANE RESOURCES QUARTERLY: BJÖRKDAL GOLD SYSTEM NOW 2.7KM STRIKE, 464M DEPTH — Open in All Directions as Mine Life Expansion Builds
snippet: Alkane Resources (ASX: ALK) reported in its September 2026 quarterly that extensional drilling at the Björkdal gold mine in Sweden has now defined the Storheden deposit over a 2.7-kilometre strike length and to 464 metres depth, with the system remaining open in all directions. Sixteen extensional diamond drill holes completed in early 2026 confirmed that high-grade gold mineralisation extends substantially beyond the resource envelope that supported mine design at restart, setting up an updated mine plan that could significantly extend Björkdal's operating life at gold prices above $4,100 per ounce — positioning Alkane as a mine life re-rating candidate ahead of a resource update.

headline: KIRKLAND LAKE DISCOVERIES HITS 73.86 G/T AT MIRADO WEST — Launches New 25,000m Program as High-Grade Ontario Camp Expands
snippet: Kirkland Lake Discoveries (TSXV: KLDC) reported 73.86 g/t gold over 1.0 metre at Mirado West and simultaneously launched a new 25,000-metre drill program to delineate what it describes as an emerging high-grade gold camp near Kirkland Lake, Ontario. The company has now intersected visible gold across a 300-metre mineralized corridor at Mirado and Mirado West, with the expanded program designed to establish geometry and continuity of a system management characterizes as having both bulk-tonnage and bonanza-grade potential in one of Canada's historically richest gold camps — a combination that attracts acquisition interest from producers hunting ounces in established infrastructure corridors.

headline: EMPEROR METALS DUQUESNE WEST: 26.3M AT 1.0 G/T FROM SURFACE, 15 HOLES PENDING — Abitibi Quebec System Continues to Build Scale
snippet: Emperor Metals (TSXV: AUOZ) released additional assays from Duquesne West in the Abitibi region of Quebec, reporting a 26.3-metre intercept at 1.0 g/t gold from approximately 40 metres depth — a near-surface, mineable-width result in a camp where major producers are aggressively acquiring development-stage ounces to feed processing infrastructure. With 15 holes still awaiting assays from the current program, the dataset is not yet complete, and the company has flagged potential for the resource footprint to expand materially at gold prices where Rouyn-Noranda district assets are attracting premium acquisition multiples.

headline: GOLD MINERS FALLING 2-5X HARDER THAN SPOT DESPITE RECORD CENTRAL BANK BUYING — The Equity-Bullion Disconnect Explained
snippet: A Discovery Alert analysis documents a significant and widening divergence: the GDX gold miners ETF is declining 2-5 times faster than spot gold even as central banks purchase bullion at record annualized rates — a supply-absorbing dynamic that has historically supported mining equity valuations. The analysis identifies three specific forces compressing gold equity multiples independent of the spot price: elevated US real yields pricing in rate-hike premium, persistently high energy input costs for producers, and sector-specific institutional outflows into Treasury alternatives. The gap between spot gold at $4,100+ and compressed equity multiples sets up a potential sharp re-rating of gold mining stocks once the FOMC cycle turns.

headline: COPPER AT $14,000 MASKS A 17-YEAR MINE DEVELOPMENT CRISIS — Record Prices Cannot Fast-Track the Permitting Calendar
snippet: A Washington Times analysis argues that copper's 2026 rally to records near $14,800 per tonne obscures a more fundamental supply crisis: the average copper mine development cycle from discovery to first production is now approximately 17 years, meaning no price signal can bring material new primary supply online before the early 2030s. The piece maps a compressed global development pipeline — where only a handful of projects are sufficiently advanced to produce within five years — against demand scenarios driven by grid electrification, EVs, and AI data centre infrastructure, concluding that the 2024-2026 commodity cycle is the prelude to a structural copper deficit that current prices still only partially price in.

headline: AURA ENERGY TIRIS URANIUM BFS: $500M NPV, 28% IRR — $349M CAPEX, Dec FID Target; Mauritania's First Mine Eyes 2028 Production
snippet: Aura Energy (ASX/AIM: AEE) released its September 2026 quarterly report confirming completion of the Tiris uranium bankable feasibility study, which delivers a post-tax NPV of US$500 million at a US$90/lb uranium price, a 28% internal rate of return, and development capital of US$349.8 million. With average C1 cash costs of US$32.53/lb over a 26-year, 1.8-million-lb/year mine life, Tiris would be one of the lowest-cost new uranium projects to reach production in this cycle. The company is targeting a December 2026 final investment decision, with US International Development Finance Corporation senior debt negotiations of US$150-170 million ongoing — putting Mauritania on the map as a new uranium jurisdiction at a time when spot uranium holds above $89/lb.
